newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela signs 17 oil operating contracts.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela signs 17 oil operating contracts.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) signed Tuesday 17 new oil and gas production contracts with private companies.

The contracts were won for a total of $2.1 billion in a public bidding round last month. They allow the private partners to reactivate ageing or abandoned oilfields in return for a share of the profits.
PDVSA expects the 17 areas to produce an extra 500-700,000 barrels per day of oil output and generate about 10,000 new jobs.

PDVSA considered the 20 areas offered too marginal to merit any of its own investment, but oil companies jumped at the chance to buy proven oil reserves with relatively low risk. Independent UK oil company Lasmo, for example, paid $453 million for just one of the contracts.
The consortia now have five working days to pay their cash bids and are expected to present their plans for field reactivation within the next three months.
It was the third such auction of oil production contracts, a key plank in Venezuela's strategy to liberalise its oil industry after 20 years of state control.
Two areas which received no bids in June's auction, Bachaquero and Cretacico, are expected to be reoffered in September or October, said PDVSA exploration director Juan Szabo.
The winning consortium for the Mata area was disqualified and this field would go under the hammer again on August 20, with a base price of $85 million, he added.
